page: Amazon Web Services r4.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance running on the Xen hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. Compute resources comprise 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores utilizing multithreading. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.25 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 45 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, while AVX-512 extensions are unsupported.

System memory totals 30.0 GB, delivering 7.62 GB per vCPU core. The hardware profile includes zero local disk storage, necessitating network-attached storage volumes for persistent data operations. GPU hardware acceleration is omitted. The instance operates with a baseline network bandwidth allocation of 1 Gbps and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place the instance in legacy computing brackets. CPU-focused benchmarks indicate lower-tier throughput, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 874.0, a multi-core score of 1871.0, and a stress-ng multi-core result of 2078.77. In memory testing, uncached large-block read operations reached 21.6 GB/sec while write operations achieved 13.47 GB/sec, though overall PassMark memory benchmarking scored 1935.76, aligning with the mid-tier baseline. Throughput measurements recorded 1.21 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.9 GB/sec in static web serving.

The hardware configuration provides high RAM capacity relative to its 4 vCPUs, making it viable for memory-bound tasks where advanced CPU performance is secondary. Appropriate workloads include distributed caching layers such as Redis or Memcached, small to mid-sized relational database engines reliant on network storage, and memory-heavy batch data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r4.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the Xen hypervisor, powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 4 dedicated vCPUs spanning 2 physical cores with hyperthreading, alongside 30.0 GB of system memory (7.62 GB per vCPU) and a 45 MB L3 cache. The server does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, relying on network storage alongside a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results reflect legacy Broadwell performance, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 1871.0 and uncached memory read bandwidth of 21.6 GB/sec, placing raw compute metrics in the lower quartiles while achieving an average PassMark memory score of 1935.76. This resource configuration is suited for memory-intensive applications with moderate processing needs, such as in-memory caches, background queue workers, and small memory-resident database systems.
